The present case stems from an accident that occurred on 09.06.2013 at around 10:20 PM near the Rajghat Ring Road FIR No. 152/2013 PS: Darya Ganj RAJ Digitally signed by RAJ KUMAR SINGH KUMAR Date: 2025.01.10 SINGH 17:03:24 +0530 Traffic Signal, within the jurisdiction of PS Darya Ganj, Delhi.

The prosecution version is that the accused, Sanjay Kumar (hereinafter "the accused"), was driving a garbage truck bearing registration no. HR-55Q-8173 in a rash and negligent manner and hit the TSR (three-wheeler scooter-rickshaw) bearing no. DL-1RE-2595 from behind/left side.
Due to the collision, the TSR overturned, resulting in grievous injuries to one Mahender Pal (PW1), including amputation of his left-hand index finger.

It is alleged that after the accident, the accused fled from the spot without rendering any assistance to the injured, thereby also attracting liability under Section 134(a)/187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

10.3 In cross-examination, PW6 denied allegations that the truck was stationary or that the accused had remained at the spot.
He affirmed fresh damage to both vehicles, consistent with a rear/side collision by the truck.
He also denied any bias in the investigation.
10.4 Observations by Court:
As the Investigating Officer, PW6's testimony is pivotal.

It is coherent,
backed by documentary evidence (site plan, seizure memos, mechanical inspection reports), and corroborates PW1, PW2, and PW3 on the accident's manner and the accused's identity.
Ct. Sachin corroborated that on 09.06.2013, he accompanied PW6 and PW5 to the accident spot, where they found the TSR and the garbage truck in damaged condition.

11.2 Observations by Court:
PW7's evidence supports the sequence of post-accident steps--registration of FIR and seizure.
No material inconsistencies arise.

12. From the duty slip (Ex. PW4/D), the statement of supervisor Deepak, and testimonies of PW4 and PW6, it emerges that accused Sanjay Kumar was the authorized driver of the garbage truck on the relevant date and time.
PW1, PW2, and PW3 consistently identified him--both in court and when he was produced at the police station.
13. PW1, PW2, and PW3 uniformly stated that the truck approached at high speed and hit the TSR from behind/left side, causing it to overturn.

The mechanical inspection reports (Ex. A6 & Ex. A7)
show fresh damage on the left front side of the truck and on the left side of the TSR.
If the truck were stationary, such an impact would be unlikely.

Further, the site plan (Ex. PW6/B) shows the truck was found some distance ahead (point B), not at the red light (point A), contradicting the accused's State vs Sanjay on 10 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123888611/

sentences.text: PW1's MLC (Ex. A3) and X-ray report (Ex. A4) confirm the amputation of his left-hand index finger, later certified as grievous.
No evidence to the contrary was offered by the defence.
15. PW1, PW2, and PW3 categorically stated that the accused abandoned his truck and fled after seeing the injuries.
This violates Section 134(a) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
PW4's statement confirms that the accused was not present at the spot later; instead, he was produced the next day by his supervisor.
16. The accused's contention that the TSR hit a stationary truck is unsupported by any independent evidence.
The mechanical inspection and location of fresh damages are consistent with the truck coming from behind.
That the TSR driver was not examined or that the TSR was allegedly overloaded does not negate the direct, consistent testimonies of PW1, PW2, and PW3.
The desire for compensation alone does not imply fabrication, especially when corroborating mechanical and site evidence exists.
17. PW1, PW2, and PW3 described a high-speed truck collision, causing the TSR to flip and leading to a significant injury (amputation).
They consistently identified the accused as the driver who fled after briefly checking the situation.
The site plan shows the garbage truck nearly 100 meters ahead from the intersection, rather than being stationary at the red light, further undermining the defence version.
FIR No. 152/2013 PS: Darya Ganj RAJ RAJ KUMAR KUMAR SINGH

entities.label: OTHER_PERSON

sentences.text: Ex. A6 and Ex. A7 confirm fresh collision damage on the left front corner of the truck and to the TSR's right side.
A stationary truck would be unlikely to sustain fresh left-front damage from a TSR presumably on its right.
This physical evidence corroborates the prosecution story that the truck was moving and rammed the TSR from behind/side.
19. PW1's ring finger amputation is evidently grievous, indicating a forceful impact.
Such injury aligns with negligent driving, rather than a minor contact with a stationary vehicle.
Section 338 IPC thus applies to causing grievous hurt by a negligent act endangering life or personal safety.

sentences.text: All occupant-witnesses stated the accused fled.
The truck was found abandoned, a fact confirmed by the Investigating Officer and constables.
This undermines the defence narrative of the accused remaining on scene.
21. The ocular testimonies of PW1, PW2, and PW3 consistently establish the negligent manner of the accused's driving.
The mechanical inspection reports and the site plan strongly corroborate the prosecution's version.
The defence has failed to create any reasonable doubt as to how the accident occurred.
The nature of PW1's injury is grievous, as confirmed by medical documents.
The accused's act of fleeing the scene without aiding the victims attracts Section 134(a)/187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Accordingly, the prosecution has proved its FIR No. 152/2013 PS: Darya Ganj RAJ Digitally signed by RAJ KUMAR SINGH KUMAR Date: 2025.01.10 SINGH 17:04:15 +0530 case beyond reasonable doubt under Sections 279/338 IPC and Section 134(a) r/w 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
22. In light of the foregoing discussion, it is evident that the accused's vehicle struck the TSR from behind without any plausible justification.
There is no indication of sudden braking, any abrupt lane change by the TSR driver, or any external factor that might have caused the collision.

The mechanical inspection further confirms that the brakes of the offending truck were functioning,
ruling out mechanical failure.
These facts and circumstances establish beyond doubt that the accused was at fault and driving negligently, thus attracting Section 279 IPC.
His negligent act resulted in grievous injury to PW1, punishable under Section 338 IPC.
Moreover, his act of fleeing the scene without offering any assistance to the injured victim clearly falls within the ambit of Section 134(a)/187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.

23. In view of the above detailed discussion and evidence on record, it is held that the accused,
Sanjay Kumar, is guilty of having driven the garbage truck no. HR-55Q-8173 in an negligent manner on 09.06.2013, thereby causing grievous hurt to PW1 (Mahender Pal) and fleeing the scene without rendering assistance.
He is accordingly convicted for offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 IPC as well as under Section 134(a)/187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
FIR No. 152/2013 PS: Darya Ganj RAJ by RAJ KUMAR KUMAR SINGH
Let the convict be heard on the question of sentence on a separate date.
A copy of this judgment be furnished free of cost to the convict, forthwith.

Sanjay Kumar, is guilty of having driven the garbage truck no. HR-55Q-8173 in an negligent manner on 09.06.2013, thereby causing grievous hurt to PW1 (Mahender Pal) and fleeing the scene without rendering assistance.
He is accordingly convicted for offences punishable under Sections 279 and 338 IPC as well as under Section 134(a)/187 of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Let the convict be heard on the question of sentence on a separate date.
A copy of this judgment be furnished free of cost to the convict, forthwith.
